title: Centrifuge Imbalance Incident — Rotor Damage and Sample Loss
description: An undergraduate research assistant loaded a centrifuge with an odd number of samples (5 tubes in a 6-position rotor) without adding a balance tube. The centrifuge was started at 12,000 RPM. After approximately 30 seconds, strong vibration was detected and the machine automatically shut down due to imbalance detection. Inspection revealed micro-fractures in one tube and rotor scoring. All samples were lost. Approximately $800 in reagents destroyed.
violations_identified: Centrifuge loaded with unbalanced samples (MAN-CENT-001 Section 2.2 and 2.3)
Odd number of samples loaded without counterbalance tube (MAN-CENT-001 Section 2.3)
Cracked tube not identified in pre-run inspection (MAN-CENT-001 Section 1.1)
root_cause: Undergraduate had not completed centrifuge safety training. Was shown 'how to use the machine' by a peer but did not receive formal training on balancing requirements. Training records were not checked before laboratory access was granted.
corrective_actions_taken: Mandatory centrifuge certification training before any independent centrifuge use
Training log now checked before granting laboratory access to new members
Quick-reference balance guide laminated and placed on centrifuge
Balance verification step added to lab onboarding checklist
outcome: No injuries. Rotor sent for professional inspection — light scoring, approved for continued use. Samples lost — experiment delayed 2 weeks.
lessons_learned: Informal peer training is insufficient for equipment operation. All equipment users must complete formal documented training. Centrifuge imbalance is a serious safety issue that can cause catastrophic rotor failure at high speeds.
content: Incident INC-2024-011: Centrifuge loaded with 5 unbalanced tubes, no balance tube added. Run at 12,000 RPM. Automatic shutdown due to imbalance. Rotor damage and sample loss. Undergraduate had not completed formal centrifuge training. Root cause: informal peer training, no training verification. Corrective actions: mandatory certification, training log checks, balance guide posted.
